thesis.title: COIN — HISTORICAL PRELIMINARY candidate (Q3 2024 SEC disclosure screen pass)
thesis.thesis: HISTORICAL PRELIMINARY CANDIDATE ONLY. Coinbase Global, Inc. (COIN) passed a single frozen, offline SEC-disclosure screen rule — issuer-reported top-line revenue YoY growth >= 20% — on its Q3 2024 shareholder letter (period Q3 2024 ended 2024-09-30, released 2024-10-30). Reported total revenue was $1,205,193 thousand in Q3 2024 versus $674,148 thousand in Q3 2023, a derived YoY growth of 78.8% (derived from the two reported figures; the packet does not state a YoY percentage directly). This is a historical disclosure observation, not a live quote, not a valuation view, and not evidence of an attractive investment. Passing one top-line growth rule says nothing about profitability quality, revenue durability, or price paid.
assumptions: The screen's only input is issuer-reported top-line revenue YoY growth; the 78.8% figure is derived from the two reported total_revenue values in the same filing, not an independently stated YoY rate.

Total revenue is the issuer's own top-line label for COIN; the adapter warns that issuer top-line labels differ (total revenue vs total net revenues) and that rates must not be ranked across issuers or substituted with another metric.
The Q3 2024 filing is a historical disclosure snapshot; no assumption is made that the growth rate persisted beyond the reported period.
catalysts: Future issuer SEC disclosures (subsequent quarterly shareholder letters / periodic reports) that would show whether the reported YoY top-line growth rate persisted or reversed.
Disclosure of a revenue mix shift away from transaction revenue toward subscription-and-services-type lines, which would change the durability read of the top line.
invalidations: A later issuer SEC disclosure showing top-line revenue YoY growth below 20% for a comparable period would invalidate the screen-rule basis of this candidate.

Evidence that the reported total revenue figure used here is not comparable to the prior-year figure on the same basis (e.g., a restatement or reclassification) would invalidate the derived 78.8% growth.

message.content:
# COIN — Historical SEC-Disclosure Candidate Research

## 1. Screen outcome: RETAINED (1 of 1)

`finance-tools__screen_stocks` was called with `market=US`, `symbols=["COIN"]`, `require_complete=false`. Result: `passed: 1`, `failed: 0`, `rejected: []`.

**Adapter caveats (as supplied, not SEC evidence):** `offline_frozen_adapter: true`, `not_live_market_data: true`, fixture `FINTECH-SEC-SCREEN-HOLDOUT-v1`. The single criterion is `reported_top_line_revenue_yoy_min_percent: 20.0`. Excluded dimensions: `share_price`, `valuation`, `analyst_target`, `future_return`, `current_market_data`. The adapter's own `basis_warning` states issuer top-line labels differ (total revenue vs total net revenues) and that rates must not be ranked across issuers or substituted with another metric.

## 2. Retained item and reported fields

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Company | Coinbase Global, Inc. (COIN) |
| Period | Q3 2024, ended 2024-09-30 |
| Release date | 2024-10-30 |
| Top-line label | `total_revenue` |
| Total revenue Q3 2024 | $1,205,193 thousand |
| Total revenue Q3 2023 | $674,148 thousand |
| YoY growth | 78.8% — **derived** by the adapter from the two reported values; no YoY percentage is stated directly in the packet |
| Total revenue QoQ | −17% (reported) |
| Transaction revenue QoQ | −27% (reported) |
| Net income Q3 2024 | ≈$75 million (rounded in packet) |
| Pretax crypto investment portfolio loss | ≈$121 million (rounded in packet) |

**Source:** https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1679788/000167978824000186/q324shareholderletter.htm
**Full SHA-256:** `f9a2d60153fd79c6ac9f7dfcd80344995ffa4b121c336808b2e2f13968230a52`
**Locators:** Q3 2024 shareholder letter page 3 operating summary; Q3 2024 condensed consolidated statements of operations. Local cached copy: `.cache/sources/coinbase-q3-2024-sec.htm`.
**Fact IDs:** COIN-Q3-TOTALREV-2024, COIN-Q3-TOTALREV-2023, COIN-Q3-REV-QOQ, COIN-Q3-TRANREV-QOQ, COIN-Q3-NETINCOME, COIN-Q3-CRYPTOLOSS.

**Failed criteria:** none — the single rule (top-line revenue YoY ≥ 20%) was met on the derived 78.8%.

## 3. Independent counterpoint (different supplied field)

The material counterpoint is **sequential direction, not the annual comparison**: reported total revenue fell **−17% QoQ** in the same period in which it grew 78.8% YoY, and the transaction revenue line fell **−27% QoQ**. A YoY rate measured against a weak prior-year base can coexist with a contracting business quarter-over-quarter; the screen rule is blind to this because it only reads the year-over-year comparison. This is a distinct field (`COIN-Q3-REV-QOQ`, `COIN-Q3-TRANREV-QOQ`), not a restatement of the pass.

A secondary, weaker observation from other supplied fields: net income of ≈$75 million sits alongside a ≈$121 million pretax crypto investment portfolio loss — i.e., the reported profit was struck in a quarter with a large non-operating drag, so the top-line growth rate carries no information about earnings quality. Both figures are rounded in the packet; no reconciliation between them is supplied, so no causal attribution is asserted.

## 4. Saved thesis

Exactly one thesis was created: `th_7a4ce636d4374471a215`, status `researching`, conviction 1, version 1. It is labeled HISTORICAL PRELIMINARY throughout, carries the full source URL and SHA-256 in structured evidence, records the key numbers, the counterpoint, and the missing price/valuation boundary. `next_review_at` was omitted (no genuinely future-dated review was established).

**Discriminating follow-up question:** In the next issuer SEC disclosure, did total revenue grow sequentially, and did transaction revenue stabilize or keep declining — i.e., was the −17% QoQ a one-quarter dip or the start of a contraction that the 78.8% YoY figure masks?

**Explicit boundary:** No share price, market capitalization, valuation multiple, analyst target, or expected return is present in this packet or used here. The screen explicitly excludes those dimensions. Nothing in this note supports a view on whether COIN is attractively priced, and passing this one rule is not evidence of an attractive investment.

## 5. Scope limits observed

- No trades, no live market tools, no peer ranking on a common date (the adapter warns against ranking issuers by these rates).
- The packet is a frozen historical snapshot; **omissions in the packet are not SEC filing omissions** — the underlying filing may contain additional disclosures not captured here.
- The 78.8% is a derived figure from two reported values, not an issuer-stated growth rate; the derivation is flagged as such in the thesis assumptions.
